haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine writes its invoices to the shadow store, for comparison only.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store and does not charge.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive days each under 0.1% mismatch, at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person asks the controller, which checks the gate and sets the flag.
haiku-low.q4: The controller's automatic rollback, when new-engine charge failures exceed 2% in any 10-minute window. Only in both or new_only, never shadow.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only with gates reset, and the rollout restarts at shadow. The forward path must be re-earned from shadow.
haiku-low.q6: Until day 35 in new_only, counted from entry, if no rollback is running then. Reason for the cutoff is not stated, beyond the lock being permanent.
haiku-low.q7: NOT STATED for how workers learn of the change. What happens to an in-flight invoice is undecided, per open question 7.
haiku-low.q8: In nightly comparison results kept per day. The controller refuses a move unless the gate is met; meeting a gate never moves the mode itself.
haiku-low.q9: The rollout controller measures the new engine's charge failure rate over any 10-minute window. Above 2% in both or new_only, it starts a rollback at Hold.
haiku-low.q10: Normal charge requests wait under the hold and are retried after it ends, none dropped. Due charges are made in Resume, before the flag is set.
haiku-low.q11: Each charge is keyed by customer and billing period, and both engines check that key against the ledger and provider. Resume charges only periods with no charge.
haiku-low.q12: Billing is left blocked: hold stays on, flag unchanged, new engine stays stopped if Resume stopped it. On-call is paged, retries, and the run restarts from Reconcile.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices to the shadow store, and never charges or writes the ledger.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store to keep it current, and does not charge.
sonnet.q3: 7 consecutive days, each with a mismatch rate under 0.1%, and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person asks the rollout controller to advance. The controller checks the gate and sets the flag, and meeting the gate never moves the mode by itself.
sonnet.q4: The controller starts one automatically when the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window. This applies only in both and new_only. In shadow, errors are recorded and never trigger a rollback.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only, with the hold and gate counters cleared. The rollout then restarts at shadow. The 7-day and 14-day counts start over, and the gates must be met again before a person advances.
sonnet.q6: Day 35 after entry into new_only, if no rollback is running when day 35 arrives. The state then becomes new_only_locked and both rollback triggers are off. The document does not give a reason for choosing day 35. It does say that skipped events expire from the 35-day usage log on day 35, and that the old engine may be decommissioned afterward.
sonnet.q7: Workers read the single global billing_mode flag in the config service. How a flag change reaches all workers at once is undecided, and so is what a worker does with a charge it started under the old value. A stale-mode worker or a half-billed handover cannot charge a period twice, because both engines check the customer-and-period key against the ledger and the payment provider before charging.
sonnet.q8: Gate evidence is the nightly comparison results, kept per day. The controller refuses to advance unless the gate is met. Only the next mode is allowed, and a person must ask for the advance.
sonnet.q9: The rollout controller detects it. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate over any 10-minute window and acts when the rate is above 2%, in both or new_only. It then starts an automatic rollback at the Hold step.
sonnet.q10: While the hold is set, workers make no normal charges. Charge requests wait and are retried after the hold ends, and none are dropped. Due charges that the rollback finds are made in the Resume step 4(b), by the old engine from the due list, using the ledger invoice amounts. These are exempt from the hold and happen before the flag is set to old_only and the hold is cleared.
sonnet.q11: Every charge is keyed by customer and billing period. Reconcile reads the ledger and asks the payment provider by that key, and Resume charges only periods with no charge for that key. The due list contains only periods with no charge. Both engines also check the key before charging.
sonnet.q12: The rollback goes to blocked and on-call is paged. The hold stays on, the flag is unchanged, and the new engine stays stopped if Resume had already stopped it. On-call retries, and the run restarts from Reconcile. This is safe because Reconcile rebuilds the due list from the ledger and provider, so charges already made are seen as charged.
